profile.summary: PredFull predicts a complete tandem mass spectrum for a peptide, not only the b and y fragment ions. The input is a table of peptides with precursor charge, fragmentation type (HCD or ETD) and normalised collision energy; the output is an MGF file of predicted peaks. The model is a residual convolutional network that predicts intensity in mass bins of 0.1 Th up to m/z 2000.

summary_quotes.text: The first model for predicting complete tandem mass spectra from peptides sequences, using a deep CNN neural network trained on over 2 million experimental spectra.
Based on the structure of the residual convolutional networks. Current precision (bin size): 0.1 Th.
The 'Type' must be HCD or ETD (in uppercase). NCE means normalized collision energy, set to 25 as default.
The prediction will NOT output peaks with M/z > 2000
The output file is in MGF format

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: PredFull treats the spectrum as a vector of mass bins rather than a list of named fragment ions. The script sets a bin width of 0.1 Th and a spectrum dimension of 20000 bins, which covers m/z up to 2000. The network is built from residual convolutional blocks, with coordinate channels added to the convolutions so position information is available, and it is trained on over 2 million experimental spectra. Predicted peaks weaker than one thousandth of the strongest peak are dropped as noise.

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: One trained model file is distributed, pm.h5, downloaded from a Google Drive folder linked in the README and placed in the repository folder. The README's update history shows the model changed over time: non-tryptic peptides were supported from May 2020, oxidised methionine from May 2021 and peptides of any length from May 2022. Only one model file is offered, so a result should name the date it was downloaded and the repository commit; this page read the repository at commit fc3641e0. The README also warns the model does not load correctly with TensorFlow earlier than 2.3.0.

sections.title: How the benchmark used it
sections.body: PepSpecBench describes PredFull as a residual CNN with squeeze-excitation of about 8.2M parameters, and treats it as a full-spectrum model whose output is projected into the benchmark's shared fragment layout. All six baselines were retrained on the benchmark data under backbone-disjoint splits, so that figure and those results describe the benchmark's retrained model, not the released pm.h5 file.
